children: , the enterprise-cybersecurity heavyweight, introduced an annual subscription that continuously hunts for exploitable weaknesses across corporate systems. Shares slipped roughly 0.7% to $390.49 at 10.35am ET time on Thursday morning.

Unit 42 Continuous Frontier AI Defense blends Anthropic's Claude Mythos 5, OpenAI's GPT-5.6-Cyber and open-weight models. The service tests applications, APIs and cloud infrastructure, then recommends code fixes or virtual patches. Pricing depends on the mix of models customers select.

The pitch is compelling: turn one-off security consulting into sticky, recurring revenue. But the valuation leaves little room for disappointment. The stock trades 67.39% above its GF Value of $233.28, signaling that investors already expect AI automation to strengthen growth and margins. Renewals will show whether those expectations are justifiedor whether model costs and human specialists keep the economics stubbornly expensive.

title: Palo Alto Drops as AI Hunts Its Own Vulnerabilities
